site: Namling basin flora, southern Lhasa block
method: CLAMP leaf physiognomy + moist static energy (GCM-derived)
notes: Abstract: Namling basin elevation 15 Myr ago 4689+/-895 m (alternative 4638+/-847 m); present altitude 4600 m; constant elevation of southern Tibet over 15 Myr. Coordinates approximate.

method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry with Rayleigh model
material_or_proxy: groundwater/pedogenic calcite and lacustrine dolomite d18O
reference_short: Currie et al. 2016 Am J Sci
notes: Abstract: late Oligocene-middle Miocene basin elevations 4.1 km +1.2/-1.6. Age bounds are late Oligocene (~26 Ma, our reading) to ~15 Ma. Supersedes the ~5.3 km pre-15 Ma estimate of Currie et al. 2005 Geology (10.1130/g21170.1; abstract not accessed). Modern basin ~4.3 km.

method: stable isotope (dD n-alkanes and siderite d18O)
material_or_proxy: plant-wax n-alkane dD; lacustrine siderite d18O
reference_short: Currie et al. 2016 Am J Sci
notes: Abstract: middle Miocene (~15 Ma) paleoelevation 5.1 km +1.3/-1.9, similar to the 5.4 km fossil-floral physiognomy estimate from the same interval.

method: stable isotope (d18O marls/concretions and n-alkane dD)
material_or_proxy: lacustrine marl; carbonate/siderite concretions; plant-wax dD
reference_short: Currie et al. 2016 Am J Sci
notes: Abstract: mean elevation 5.5 km +1.4/-2.0 at ~5 Ma; modern basin ~4.3 km, allowing >1 km loss since the early Pliocene by extensional collapse.

method: clumped isotope (Delta47) + d18O paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: Eocene to Pliocene Oiyug estimates ~6.5-4.1 km; high elevation by at least ca. 30 Ma. Age bounds here span Oligocene-Pliocene (our reading of 'Eocene to Pliocene'; per-sample ages not in abstract). elev_m midpoint (ours). CrossRef issue year 2017 (online), print 2018.

method: clumped isotope (Delta47) + d18O paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: Paleocene to Eocene Nianbo Fm 4.4 km +1.3/-1.7, extending high elevation to pre-collision (Lhasaplano). Age bounds approximate (abstract gives epoch only). Botsyun et al. 2019 argue Eocene d18O-based altimetry in Asia is biased high; the Delta47 temperature component makes this row more robust than d18O-only estimates.

method: clumped isotope (Delta47) + d18O paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: Eocene Pana Fm 4.1 km +1.2/-1.6. Age bounds approximate (abstract gives epoch only). Same Eocene-bias caveat as Nianbo row.

method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry
notes: Value 4.5+/-0.4 km at ~56 Ma (Paleocene-Eocene) taken from a secondary citation (Frontiers in Earth Science 2021, 10.3389/feart.2021.810931); original abstract not accessed. Age bounds approximate. Weak: Eocene d18O altimetry in Asia contested by Botsyun et al. 2019 (convective precipitation, air-mass mixing, aridity).

method: leaf physiognomy (paleoenthalpy) with U-Pb dated flora
notes: Abstract: proto-Himalaya ~1 km in the late Paleocene (ca. 56 Ma) against a ~4 km proto-Tibetan Plateau. Error not given in abstract, hence weak. Coordinates approximate.

method: leaf physiognomy (paleoenthalpy) with U-Pb dated flora
notes: Abstract: ~2.3 km at the beginning of the Miocene (Qiabulin flora 21-19 Ma); Himalaya at least ~5.5 km by ca. 15 Ma. Error not given in abstract, hence weak. Coordinates approximate.

site: Mount Everest region, South Tibetan detachment shear zone
method: stable isotope (dD) of syn-kinematic hydrous minerals vs foreland d18O
notes: Abstract: mean elevation >=5000 m for the Everest area in the late Early Miocene (meteoric water dD -156+/-5 permil vs near-sea-level foreland). Minimum only; upper bound open. Age bounds approximate for 'late Early Miocene'.

method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry
material_or_proxy: fluvial and lacustrine carbonate d18O (-16 to -23 permil)
notes: NEAR-MODERN: abstract states meteoric water values similar to modern, so southern Tibet attained its current elevation before E-W extension began at 10-11 Ma (Tetang Fm); Thakkhola Fm younger than 8 Ma. No numeric elevation in abstract; Rowley et al. 2001 EPSL (10.1016/s0012-821x(01)00324-7) recast these data with a thermodynamic model (abstract not accessed).

method: stable isotope (d18O) of mollusc aragonite
reference_short: Saylor et al. 2009 Am J Sci
notes: NEAR-MODERN or higher: abstract states surrounding peaks were at least as high as today and possibly up to 1.5 km higher during 9.2 to <1 Ma; climate cold and arid since >=9 Ma. No absolute value in abstract.

method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: arid climate and high paleoelevation (4.5-5 km, comparable to today) by 26 Ma, from accurately dated paleosol carbonate. elev_m midpoint (ours).

method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry (thermodynamic model)
notes: Abstract: surface of Tibet >4 km for at least the past 35 Myr. Contested: Fang et al. 2020 re-dated the section (high elevations at ~26 Ma, <2.3 km at 39.5 Ma), Su et al. 2019 palm fossils, and Botsyun et al. 2019 Eocene isotope bias. Coordinates from Su et al. 2019.

method: stable isotope paleoaltimetry re-dated by magnetostratigraphy and radiometric ages
notes: Abstract: central Tibet generally low (<2.3 km) at 39.5 Ma on the revised chronology. Maximum only. Weak: Eocene isotope-based value, see Botsyun et al. 2019.

method: stable isotope paleoaltimetry re-dated by magnetostratigraphy and radiometric ages
notes: Abstract: high (3.5-4.5 km) at ~26 Ma; uplift of a low, E-W elongated Eocene valley by the early Miocene. elev_m midpoint (ours).

method: fossil indicator (palm leaves; freezing intolerance) + modelled lapse rate
notes: Abstract: palm leaves from 25.5+/-0.5 Ma paleolake beds at 4655 m today; valley floor <2.3 km a.s.l., flanked by >4 km mountains. Weak because the age conflicts with Fang et al. 2020, whose revised chronology implies the palm beds are older than 25.5 Ma.

method: marine fossil indicator (foraminifera) + carbonate d18O
material_or_proxy: foraminifera (Lagena laevis) in lacustrine beds; carbonate d18O
notes: Abstract: lagoon/estuarine foraminifera in upper Eocene strata imply the northern Lhasa terrane was near sea level; authors propose storm-surge transport into low freshwater lakes, supported by relatively positive d18O. Treated as sea-level datum but weak because the marine fauna is inferred to be transported. Age bounds = late Eocene (our reading). Coordinates approximate.

site: Hoh Xil basin (Fenghuoshan Group), northern Tibet
method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: hypsometric mean elevation of the drainage basins feeding the middle Eocene Hoh Xil lakes <=~2 km. Contested: Quade et al. 2011 Am J Sci (10.2475/02.2011.01) recalculated with higher carbonate formation temperatures and latitude correction and obtained elevations much closer to modern. Age bounds approximate (middle Eocene).

method: isotope-enabled GCM reassessment of published d18O paleoaltimetry
notes: Abstract: d18O paleoaltimetry not applicable in Eocene Asia (convective precipitation, air-mass mixing, aridity); model-data comparison suggests the plateau reached only low to moderate (<3000 m) elevation in the Eocene. Not a new proxy record; included to bracket the debate. Contested in comments/replies (Science 2019).
